scope: Manual alignment-only repair of Likutay Tefilos I:1; hashes are regression locks, not automatic semantic scoring.
source_disposition: Original English 3–6 contains the prayer once. Original2/7/8 duplicate that text with encoded language-menu prefixes. Preserve original English exactly apart from boundary whitespace; replace only heading2 with 1 Tishrei. Both Hebrew representations and every other field unchanged.
review: Parent manual reading plus independent complete 25-pair semantic/philological review; source spans checked independently. No truncation, displacement or duplicate prayer prose introduced. Not certification of a newly literal translation.

inherited_reservations.en_exact: lishma [for its own sake / for the sake of the Shechina]
inherited_reservations.note: The second alternative is an interpretive gloss, not words explicitly in this Hebrew clause. It is visibly bracketed and inherited unchanged. Preserve it in this alignment-only repair; this review does not certify it as a literal lexical equivalent.

inherited_reservations.en_exact: our many sins and transgressions and iniquities
inherited_reservations.note: All three sin categories remain, but transgressions/iniquities is not the usual ordered English mapping of avonot/peshaim. Also מאד מאד is conveyed intensively by profoundly/greatly rather than by literal verbal repetition. These are source translation precision reservations, not loss or displacement introduced by pairing.

inherited_reservations.en_exact: And fulfill for us the verse that is written:
inherited_reservations.note: "for us" is supplied by the inherited English; the Hebrew has no explicit lanu here. No repair-induced addition: the source span and its placement are exact.

Akum is the traditional acronym for worshippers of stars/constellations (idolaters); "nations" is broader and less explicit than that wording. The first occurrence retains [akum], the second repeats nations without the acronym. This is inherited, not a repair-created softening. All requests to nullify/subdue opponents and the neither-above-nor-below negations remain intact. Also glory [keren] glosses the horn metaphor rather than literally rendering horn. Preserve source text in this scoped repair; do not claim a newly literal philological edition.
